findings.reason: The exclusively created temporary file is closed, read back by pathname, then renamed. A writer with access to the package directory can change the pathname after validation. A deterministic I/O-interference probe confirmed modified bytes can replace the old manifest. The CLI subsequently verifies but cannot retroactively preserve the prior manifest.
findings.action: Keep sealing restricted to a trusted quiescent directory. Follow-up hardening should avoid pathname reopen where possible and address ownership through replacement; do not claim atomicity across mutable package inputs. No browser-runtime exploit established.

findings.reason: Before bindings[name] assignment, names.filter only allows assertInteractionSourceFidelity and semanticInjectionText. Neither prototype keys nor arbitrary names can pass. Names and import paths come from local panel source; actual imports resolve to core/injection.js and host/check-source.js.
findings.action: No fix required for the reported property injection; preserve allowlist.

findings.reason: argv[1] versus import.meta.url identifies direct CLI invocation, not authorization. --seal is an explicit local maintainer action subject to filesystem permissions. The inventory and truncate-first defects are fixed in this commit; a separate local filesystem race remains.
findings.action: Keep the entrypoint guard. No authentication bypass fix or suppression required.
